title: When We Move Forward
subtitle: An expensive group photo. Usually found in a weathered old frame.

trails.title: /lo/ - The Spread of Enigmafication
trails.description: The pale green characters pulse with emotion. Making sense of what they're saying is going to take all your cunning.

content.text:
0001 Anonymous No.95025535 ▶
Just had a two-year project canceled. Soon I too will be able to hide out in my room all day playing Sudoku. Not sad about this at all.

0002 Anonymous No.95025586 ▶ >>95025620
I wouldn't start celebrating just yet. It looks like you're about to lose your vacation time since there's a shortage of staff everywhere.

0003 Anonymous No.95025620 ▶ >>95025867
>>95025586
What are they gonna do? It's not like a simple number theory major like me can contribute to rebuilding in the wake of the "Storm." Nothing's going to stop me from going on vacation, nothing!

0004 Anonymous No.95025631 ▶ >>95025718
Would you look at that? The Enigmafication is spreading nicely. Good. At this rate, I'll have the entire Laplace break room all to myself.

0005 Anonymous No.95025718 ▶ >>95025961
>>95025631
As more people start slacking off, supplies will be cut too. You might get to hog all the Daily Meals from all of Laplace, but that's probably the best you'll do.

0006 Anonymous No.95025867 ▶
>>95025620
You know, it'd be hilarious if a bunch of random numbers and formulas turned out to be the key to defeating the "Storm," and you got roped into nonstop 24/7 work trying to crack it, with Madam Lucy interrogating you three times a day about your progress.

0007 Anonymous No.95025961 ▶
>>95025718
That sounds absolutely disgusting. I need a nap just at the thought of that.

0008 Anonymous No.95026012 ▶
Oh, and as part of the "humanitarian" gesture, I'll make sure your voice gets added to the machine too.

0009 Anonymous No.95026078 ▶ >>95026278
Well isn't that something? There are still poor souls who didn't get a vacation even at a time like this, with all these non-essential projects getting cut?

0010 Anonymous No.95026278 ▶ >>95026293
>>95026078
There's plenty. Like John from the medical team, John from the mechanical engineering group, and John from materials science ... Basically, every non-theoretical department is pulling all-nighters to rebuild Laplace under Madam Lucy's brand of ruthless pragmatism.

0011 Anonymous No.95026293 ▶
>>95026278
It really makes you wonder if the "Storm" was part of a conspiracy by the Johns to steal funding from the rest of the teams and justify their overtime pay. Coincidence? I think not!

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Will I ever have the chance to return to Utrennyaya?
Hissabeth pushes the door open just in time to catch this scene. She lingers nearby, curious, watching the girl receive her answer.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: We can talk about that in the future.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Of course, we will keep in touch. You and Voyager can pay us a visit whenever you like.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: The girl's called Voyager, madam. She's clever, quiet, doesn't eat much. You-You will take her in too, won't you?
Pointer doesn't object. She runs a brief analysis and concludes that the company of a peer could help ease the pressures of Kiperina's training.
After listening carefully, Mr. Kozlov pats Kiperina's shoulder.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: I always hoped you would settle down and live a comfortable life. Promise me, you'll do your best, Alia.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Yes, Mr. Kozlov.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, you've finally reached an agreement. Cool, looks like I won't have to do any more explaining.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: If you're saying goodbye soon, maybe you ought to consider bringing her a parting gift. She looks like she could use one.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Yeah, something to remind her of home.
Name Day picks up the thread without missing a beat.
Windsong steps forward just in time, joining Kiperina's side, and Hissabeth trails off.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Or maybe you can offer a few words of encouragement? What do you say?
Mr. Kozlov spies Kiperina rubbing the device in her hands with her pinky—the one Windsong had lent her earlier. He knows her well enough to understand the meaning: nervous.
He has no idea about the device's exact value, but he's certain it's not something you'd easily find in a circus.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Right, right, a gift. I-I'll need some time to prepare it.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Let's make a deal, shall we? You'll get your gift next time you pay a visit to the Utrennyaya.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: That way, you'll keep us in mind and come home again one day. I was worried you might not want to travel such a long way for us.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I will, Mr. Kozlov. I'll find my way back to Utrennyaya even if you've moved to the other end of the world.
She struggles to lift the parcel Mr. Kozlov gave her. Name Day quickly steps in to assist her in placing it on the table.
"Time flies." The thought pops into Mr. Kozlov's head, but what he says out loud has nothing to do with it.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Hahaha, that's my girl.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Remember what I said? Do the best that you can and have no regrets.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Natalya and I don't have to worry about you, do we?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: No.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I'll give my best performance here, like I always did with Utrennyaya.
Almost like she's trying to convince herself, she nods twice in a row and makes a solemn promise in her most serious tone.
A question rises up in her, just below the surface. How can she be sure? She chooses not to ask.
June 1987, Plesetsk Cosmodrome

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: How do you feel? Intense nausea is common for the first few months of zero-g training.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: *pant* I think I'm fine.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: You're very kind to ask, ma'am.
Her first training session was rough and more than a little messy, causing her to throw up.
Pointer helped her to the infirmary. Once she could breathe again, she stammered out a request—just like the one she made today.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I'm ready for more.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You're at this again? Hissabeth already checked your vitals and arcane skill test reports. Her conclusion was clear: You need to rest and recover before we begin again.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: If you push yourself too hard and become too sick to perform the mission, that won't help us either.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: But I can do more. All I need is a bit more training. I need to perform flawlessly.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: We don't need "flawless," not at the cost of your health. We need "satisfies all requirements." Nothing more.
She adjusts her tone, searching her mind for something that might qualify as comfort or encouragement.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You're already doing better than we anticipated.
She fears the words come out too flat, but Kiperina shakes her head sincerely.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Thank you. But I still haven't memorized the flight procedures, and I'm still struggling with my arcane skill.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Maybe I can ask Ms. Windsong to give me another ley lines lesson. That's not "pushing myself," is it?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: That's acceptable, but you will ensure you get a minimum of eight hours of sleep every day.
Pointer gives in. She too had once been hell-bent on proving herself.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: And promise me you'll eat well and never skip meals.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Yes, ma'am. Ms. Hissabeth said there would be a team-building dinner tonight. I'll attend it and train for another half an hour after we come back.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: No. That's not what I meant.
There are few tasks more difficult than instructing a child who is too mature for her own good.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: *sigh* Anyway, go change. We'll go together.
Of all the restaurants in Mirny, this one does the best business, thanks in no small part to Hissabeth.
With all those mouths to feed, food has always been a vital part of her lifestyle, one that she is only too eager to share with her team.
Plus, the tables here are big enough for everyone in their group to have a seat.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We sat here when we first met, non?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I think so. This table seems a bit too small now.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Well, there's strength in numbers.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Yet everything now depends on our brave astronaut. How's your arcane skill training?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Not bad, I guess. Ms. Windsong is a wise teacher.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Haha, I'm glad I've learned something from my experience with Vila. I hope you'll get to know her one day.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: You'll have plenty of time to make friends once you return from your mission.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Looking forward to it. But first I have to go back to the circus. I think Mr. Kozlov will have my gift prepared by then. I'm sure he will.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Though, he didn't come to see me and Voyager this week.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: He has a whole circus to run, and you're busy with training. It's hard to find a good time when you're both free.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Perhaps he didn't want to make you homesick, but I'm sure he misses you a lot.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Mirny isn't far from here. You should go back and visit sometime. No one will blame you if you take a break for a few hours.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I am able to drive you to town, if you need.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Just submit your schedule two days in advance. I will set some time aside for a short trip.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Thank you. But I think it'll have to wait until the project's over.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Mr. Kozlov said I would always be able to visit him in the future. Besides, he needs time to prepare the gift.
Not everyone is interested in the still distant future. Kiperina's friend, at least, is more focused on what's right in front of her.
She taps the edge of the small vessel, smiling at the crisp, metallic sound it makes.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: Err. Don't do that. The echo from that sound makes me dizzy.
She pulls her hand back and watches until confirming the little creature is friendly.
Then she reaches out again, trying to figure out how to get along with it.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Voyager?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Don't get distracted. They've almost finished the food.
Name Day swaps the food around the table, pushing two still-full plates to the middle.
Cold scales press against Kiperina's wrist.

items.speaker: Snake I
items.text: Feel like a drink? Here, we've got some hot milk or warm apple cider. Pick one.
Dragging a cup behind it, the snake leaves splotches of spilled drink all across the table.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Milk will be fine. Thank you.
Kiperina passes another cup to Voyager. She mimics the others by lifting the cup, first in both hands and then just one.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Let's have a toast, friends. To our new team, though no one knows for sure whether our project will succeed or is doomed to fail catastrophically.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Together, we're working towards the future, cheers!
A friendly signal. A quiet promise of unity.
A turning point in any story or relationship, from a stranger to a colleague, and eventually—

Друг/Товарищ.
"Friend/Comrade."

items.speaker: All
items.text: Cheers!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Having said that, the odds are in our favor. Even though Laplace is no longer in its prime, it still has the best technology and the finest scientists.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The finest scientists? You mean us? I couldn't agree more. I've always believed that perseverance is the most basic fundamental quality that any researcher should possess.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Perseverance ... There's only one thing that I think we should persevere with: our efforts to return to the future.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Didn't know you Laplace researchers missed the good old days so much.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Laugh if you want, but you can't deny that our era was better than this one.
Kiperina keens her ears in, trying to catch each word. The room is warm, and the conversation at their table easy and relaxed. The question she's been keeping down finally bubbles out of her mouth.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: What was the future like?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I've read through the manual for temporary employees. The data we're going to collect may help people get back the things that they lost, right? From the futures that you've been to.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: What's Leningrad like in 1999? Were there any circus shows in your era?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Does that mean everything was better than it is now? I have trouble imagining it. Were there sweets for everyone and stores that never ran out of food?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Things were much better then, well, except for the study of ley lines. It was still struggling as a scientific pursuit, especially when it came to attracting new students. Though, even now its only student seems to lack much interest in it.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Th-That's not true! Sorry, I'm just having difficulty focusing on it with all the other demands on my time.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: It's okay. Ms. Windsong was only making a joke at the expense of her very overworked student.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: It's true things were nicer in the future. I do miss the sweets, and that the shops were never empty.
Every witness seems to offer her the same promise: it's worth it.
Life should move forward, not stay stuck in the past.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Amazing! I'm sure we'll make it back one day!
This time, she raises her cup first.
